lessons.title: Choose a voice and a move
lessons.outcome: Develop a character with voice and movement.
lessons.goal: I can choose a voice and a move for a made-up role.
success: I can try two ways to say a line.
I can choose one small move.
I can show my choice and why.
words: The part you play in a story.
The sound you use to say words.
How fast you speak or move.

artist_cards.description: The Keeper says, "My table has moved." The words come fast. The hands stop by the chest. The Keeper then asks, "Can you help?"
artist_cards.notice: Are the first words fast or slow?
artist_cards.prompt: What small hand move did the Keeper use?
artist_cards.model_answer: The first words are fast. The hands stop by the chest. The move is small and stays in the performer's own space.

artist_cards.description: The Keeper says the same words slowly. One open hand points to an empty spot. There is a short pause. The Keeper then asks, "Can you help?"
artist_cards.notice: What has changed in this version?
artist_cards.prompt: Which version fits your Keeper? Why?
artist_cards.model_answer: The words are slower. The open hand points to a spot and there is a pause. Either version is a valid choice if the pupil gives a reason.

staff_guidance.plain_language: Resilience can mean pausing, asking for help, changing a plan and trying again. It does not mean hiding feelings, tolerating harm or performing through pain.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. The lesson contributes evidence towards the award; it does not confer the award. Optional next level work in GROW adds skills planning, reflection and sharing evidence for later review. It is not a separate requirement for Explore success.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: A clear tiny model is enough. Read the original lines and show a small hand action. Compare two versions. Assess an intentional skill choice and explanation, not acting confidence or a polished performance. Do not use accents, impersonations or a disability to signify a character.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Use the invented changed-table story. No personal story is needed. Offer seated movement, silent direction, a private adult audience and a pass on live peer performance. Voice and taps stay at talking level or below. Agree an open-hand stop signal and quiet return cue. No sudden sounds, contact, running, raised platforms, blindfolds or lifts.
staff_guidance.safety: Clear a small working space. Keep both feet supported if seated. Use hands within each person's own space. No touching another performer or taking a prop from them. Sound is optional; stop on the agreed signal. Pupils can direct the adult to perform their chosen pace and movement. Record that as directed evidence, not a vocal or physical skill the pupil personally demonstrated.
prompt_ladder: Point to the instruction or place.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Pre-teach role, pace, pause and choice with a brief model. Show one instruction at a time. Offer two pace choices, rehearse once, then fade the prompt. Use a tiny plan with beginning, change and response.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Give processing time. Accept pointing to a pace word, signing, a phrase, a sketch or exact words scribed by an adult. Read the record back for confirmation. Do not judge accent, eye contact or facial expression.
adaptations.semh: Keep the story fictional and low stakes. A pause, a change in method or a request for help can be the character's response. Let pupils choose the role, amount of performance and audience. Follow the agreed pause-and-return route.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Offer seated hand movement and no sound. A pupil may direct an adult voice or movement. Keep each person in their own space; use no compulsory facial expression or posture. Ask before handling a pupil's work.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Explain pace as how fast we speak or move. Accept first planning in a familiar language and check the intended meaning before adding English labels. The pupil may use a short English phrase or direct a partner.

misconceptions.claim: A character needs a loud voice or a large action.
misconceptions.correction: A short clear phrase and a small deliberate action can communicate a role. Keep sound at a comfortable level.

misconceptions.claim: Feedback tells a performer what they must feel.
misconceptions.correction: Describe a feature that was seen or heard. Ask the maker about their intention and let them choose a change.

misconceptions.claim: A teacher example can fill a missing arts-log entry.
misconceptions.correction: Record only what the pupil actually chose, tried, directed, made or shared, with the real date and support used.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Performers and sound makers practise a skill, take turns and use feedback to refine a piece.

ta_focus.I do: Make the change in pace or movement easy to notice. Invite a point or sign for the check after the model.
ta_focus.We do: Give each pupil one choice. If the hinge response is uncertain, model one clear contrast before returning to the shared try.
ta_focus.Independent: Use the prompt ladder. Record what support was actually used. Return the next choice to the pupil after a first-step model.

lessons.evidence: Keep a dated arts-log entry and a precise observation of a real trial. Record what the pupil performed or directed, the chosen feature, reason, feedback and support actually used. A photograph or recording is optional and follows local consent procedures. No supplied teacher model counts as pupil evidence.
lessons.artist_use_note: The two performance examples are invented classroom demonstrations, not accounts of real artists or an arts encounter. Read or demonstrate them in the room. They can support comparison and skills exploration only.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Pick a role: Keeper or Helper.
You can sit, point, speak, sign or direct.
This is a made-up story.
stages.say: Our Keeper comes to work at a table. The table has moved. That is our made-up change. You can play the Keeper or help me play it. We will keep our hands in our own space and stop at my open hand.
stages.good: Pupils choose or confirm a role or a directing job. The stop signal and working space are clear.
stages.fallback: Offer the two role words and ask for a point. The adult performs while the pupil directs.
stages.answer: Either role or a directing role is valid. Do not require a pupil to share a real experience of change.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Hear: My table has moved.
Hear it fast. Hear it slow.
Point: fast or slow?
stages.say: I say the same line in two ways, both at a quiet talking level. First fast, then slow. Which one was slow? We have changed pace, not the words.
stages.good: Pupils identify a contrast in pace by word, gesture or choice.
stages.fallback: Say just "It has moved" twice with a very clear contrast. Use one finger for fast and two for slow.
stages.answer: The second version is slow in this model. A quiet voice can be fast or slow. Loudness and pace are different.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch the two Keeper versions.
Hear one line in two ways.
Watch one small hand move.
Which way might you choose?
stages.say: I read or show example A, then B. I choose the slow line, "My table has moved," and an open hand to the empty spot. I want my Keeper to take time to look. Another Keeper could choose fast words. Check: did I change the words, the pace, or both?
stages.good: Adult compares two versions and gives one reason. Check after the model: pupils identify that pace changed and the words stayed the same.
stages.fallback: Use only the short line and an open hand. Point to fast or slow and let the pupil choose the adult's next version.
stages.answer: The words stayed the same; the pace changed. Both choices can work. A character's feeling cannot be known just from a hand shape.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Choose fast or slow for our Keeper.
Choose one small move.
Try the line and move once.
Say: We chose ___ because ___.
stages.say: Let us choose the pace first. Now choose an open hand or hands resting still. I perform the class choice, then we try the other pace. Hinge: which helps our Keeper look before asking for help? Give a reason. If the reason is unclear, I show the slow version with a pause and we choose again.
stages.good: Each pupil makes or confirms a choice. The class links a feature to an intention; no feeling is imposed.
stages.fallback: Adult offers two choices and performs the confirmed direction. A pupil can point rather than act.
stages.answer: A slow line and pause might show looking before asking. A fast line could also fit if the pupil explains a different intended Keeper. Accept a reason about a visible or heard feature.

stages.name: Create
pupil: In your book or arts log, pick a role.
Try the line fast, then slow.
Try a small move with the line.
Keep one voice and one move.
Say or show why.
stages.say: Use the Keeper line, "My table has moved," or the Helper line, "We can find a new spot." Practise each at two paces at talking level or below. Add one small hand move or a clear still pause. Keep the version you choose. Work with a partner, adult or alone. A silent director can choose the adult's voice and move. Record those directions as your evidence.
stages.good: Two actual pace trials, one chosen pace and movement or stillness, and a confirmed reason. A directed performance is labelled as directed rather than performed by the pupil.
stages.fallback: Pupil points to a pace and a hand choice. Adult performs both trials and asks which to keep. Record the pupil's exact confirmed choice.
stages.answer: Example only: I chose slow words and an open hand because my Keeper looks first. Any deliberate safe choice with a reason is valid. Do not copy this model as the pupil's work.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Show your line and move, or direct it.
A partner says: I notice ___.
Tell us your choice.
Put your work in a safe place.
stages.say: Share with one partner or just me. The listener names one thing they saw or heard: "I notice a pause." The maker says whether that was planned. Use the final two minutes to put pencils away and store each real log for tomorrow.
stages.good: A factual observation is shared respectfully and the maker confirms an intention. Work is kept for lesson two.
stages.fallback: Adult describes the performance neutrally and asks for yes, no or a changed word. No peer audience is required.
stages.answer: Useful feedback: I heard the words get slower. Avoid claims about what the pupil or character must feel.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: My role is ___.
I tried fast and slow words.
I chose ___ and ___ because ___.
Next time I will ___.
stages.say: Point to or tell me your real choice. I can write your words and read them back. Mark if you performed or directed. Keep your two trials in a brief note so we can use them next time.
stages.good: Dated entry shows the role, two actual trials, chosen voice and movement, reason, and support used.
stages.fallback: Use one confirmed choice at a time. Adult writes a short witnessed note with the pupil's own words or gesture meaning.
stages.answer: Example only: I directed the Keeper. I chose slow words and a still pause. Next time I will add the help line. Record only what happened today.

Supported: Tell the adult: fast or slow.
Choose an open hand or still hands.
Try both ways. Keep one. Say or show why.
Independent: Add one small move or pause.
Keep a voice and move. Log your reason.
Aspire: Change the pause or one hand move.
Say how the new choice changes the role.
Keep a note of both real tries.

log: My chosen voice and move are ___.
misconceptions: A good role needs a shout
Use a clear voice at talking level or below. A quiet line can show a clear role.
Fast words always mean cross
Ask the maker what they meant. The same pace can have more than one meaning.
Directing means I did nothing
Keep the pupil's real pace and movement choices. Label the evidence as direction.
kit: For three to four pupils: one book or arts log and pencil each.
Two original example cards and the Keeper and Helper lines, read aloud if needed.
A clear seated or standing space with no contact or running.
No costume, prop, device, sound playback or recording is needed.
Keep each pupil's dated choice note for lesson two.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Say the Keeper line quickly at quiet talking level. Keep hands by the chest.
15 to 30 seconds
Say the same line slowly. Open one hand towards an empty spot.
30 to 45 seconds
Say: I choose slow words because my Keeper looks first. Show a short pause.
45 to 60 seconds
Ask pupils to choose fast or slow and perform their choice once.
models: Teacher model only: My Keeper says the line slowly and shows an open hand. The Keeper takes time to look.
Teacher model only: I directed the Helper to speak slowly and stay still. I wanted the words to be clear.
lessons.cover: Read the two original Keeper examples, show fast and slow speech at quiet talking level, then let each pupil choose a pace and a small movement. Use the seven stages. Pupils keep a real dated choice note for lesson two. A pupil may direct the adult or share privately. No costume, prop or internet is required.

cold_call.middle: What move did you choose with the line?
cold_call.higher: How did that voice and move help show your role?

lessons.title: Keep and change your character
lessons.outcome: Develop a character with voice and movement.
lessons.goal: I can use my voice and move in a short scene.
success: I can use my chosen voice and move.
I can try one helpful change.
I can log what I kept and why.
words: One short part of a story.
A sign that it is your turn.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your real choice note.
Pick act, speak, sign or direct.
We use the same made-up story.
stages.say: Yesterday our Keeper found the table had moved. Find your choice of voice and move. If you were away or the note is missing, make a fresh fast and slow test now; date it today. You do not need to pretend to remember.
stages.good: Pupils retrieve actual prior choices or make a clearly dated fresh test. Participation and stop routes are confirmed.
stages.fallback: Read the role lines and offer fast or slow. Adult makes the selected trial while the pupil directs.
stages.answer: Missing work is a fresh starting point, not a failure. Record the real date and support.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Try your line and move once.
A partner watches or listens.
Say: I notice ___.
stages.say: Use a short warm-up at quiet talking level. One pupil says or directs a line; the other notices the pace, pause or small move. Then swap, or work privately with me.
stages.good: Pupils recall a deliberate feature and give a neutral observation.
stages.fallback: Adult performs the pupil's confirmed choice and the pupil points to the feature they notice.
stages.answer: An observation names a feature: I notice slow words or I notice an open hand. It need not judge the performer.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch our three-line scene.
Keeper: My table has moved.
Helper: We can find a new spot.
Keeper: I will try that.
Hear a pause. See a small move.
stages.say: I show the whole tiny scene once, with a pause before the last line. The Keeper looks to a new spot with one open hand. Now I rush the last line, then try the pause again. I keep the pause so the response is clear. Check: which part did I change?
stages.good: Adult models a complete three-line scene, one revision and a reason. Pupils identify the pause as the changed feature.
stages.fallback: Read one line at a time. Use a hand cue for each turn. Let the pupil direct the pace of the last line.
stages.answer: The pause before the final line changed. The story words stayed the same. A change is useful when it helps the intended scene.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Pick Keeper or Helper.
Use a hand cue for each turn.
Try the three lines together.
Choose one part to make clear.
stages.say: I cue one turn at a time with an open hand. Use your chosen pace and move. Hinge: if both roles speak at once, what could help? Choose a hand cue or a louder voice. If anyone chooses louder, model the same sound level with a clear cue and try again.
stages.good: Each role has a clear turn. Pupils choose a cue or pause to help turn-taking, not louder sound.
stages.fallback: Adult reads all lines while pupils direct turns with one, two and three fingers. Keep the same story order.
stages.answer: A hand cue or pause helps us take turns. A louder voice does not tell us whose turn comes first. Rehearse the cue if turns are still unclear.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Use your voice and move in the scene.
Try it once with your partner or adult.
Hear: I notice ___.
Change one part if it helps.
Try it again. Keep your choice.
stages.say: Work in pairs, with an adult, or as a director. Use the three original lines or make your own short help line. First try the scene. A listener names one feature. Choose one change in pace, pause, movement or turn cue. Try again. Keep a brief note of the first try and final choice. No performance to the whole class is needed.
stages.good: A real first try and a revised try show one intentional skill choice. The pupil can say or show what changed and why. Directed evidence is labelled accurately.
stages.fallback: Adult performs both versions under pupil direction. Ask: keep the pause or change it? Record the confirmed choice and reason.
stages.answer: Example only: We added a pause before "I will try that" so the new plan was clear. A pupil may keep the first version if they can explain why it works.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Show a short part or direct it.
Listener: I notice ___.
Maker: I kept ___ because ___.
Store the real log.
stages.say: Show one line or a short section to your chosen listener. The listener names a feature, and the maker explains one kept or changed choice. Reserve the last two minutes to return pencils and put logs in order.
stages.good: Sharing is accessible and consensual. Feedback connects to a real feature, and the maker's choice is kept.
stages.fallback: The adult gives a neutral observation; pupil confirms by word, gesture or point. Sharing may be private.
stages.answer: A useful reply is: I kept the slow line because it was clear. Both keeping and changing can be a reasoned decision.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: My role was ___.
I used ___ voice and ___ move.
I tried a change in ___.
I kept ___ because ___.
stages.say: Complete today's real log. Record what you performed or directed, one change you tested and your reason. I can scribe and read it back. Pick one next step for next week's group story.
stages.good: Dated arts-log entry distinguishes the actual trial, choice, reason and support. A next step points towards clear group turns.
stages.fallback: Pupil selects one feature and confirms a short adult note. Leave an honest gap if a part was not tried.
stages.answer: Example only: I used slow words and an open hand. I added a pause to help my turn. Next time I will watch the cue.

Supported: Pick your role or direct the adult.
Use the three short lines with hand cues.
Try one pause or move change.
Keep your choice. Tell or show why.
Independent: Use your chosen voice and move.
Try the scene with clear turns.
Get one notice from a listener.
Test one change and log your reason.
Aspire: Keep the role clear when the plan changes.
Test two ways to cue the last line.
Explain which cue helps the scene most.

misconceptions: The best scene is the loudest
A clear pace and turn cue can help the scene at quiet talking level.
I must take every piece of feedback
Choose one helpful idea, test it and give your own reason.
The scene must be long
Three clear lines can show a change and a response.
kit: For three to four pupils: books or arts logs, pencils and yesterday's actual choice notes if available.
Three original scene lines read or displayed one at a time.
A clear seated or standing working space; no props or costumes needed.
A pupil can direct the adult, and no recording is required.
Keep today's trial and reason for next week's story sequence.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Read all three lines, using a hand cue for each turn.
15 to 30 seconds
Repeat the last Keeper line with no pause, then with one short pause.
30 to 45 seconds
Say: I keep the pause because the new choice is clear.
45 to 60 seconds
Ask the pupil to cue the adult's three turns and confirm the pace.
models: Teacher model only: I kept the Keeper's slow line and open hand. I added a pause so the last choice was clear.
Teacher model only: I directed the three turns with my hand. The listener noticed the cue. I kept it because no lines overlapped.
lessons.cover: Retrieve real prior choice notes or make a fresh two-pace trial dated today. Read the three original lines. Model a pause and turn cue, then support one real rehearsal, feedback, change and repeat. Keep evidence of performed or directed choices separately and accurately. Use a private listener if preferred.

cold_call.foundation: Whose turn comes after the Keeper?
cold_call.middle: Which pause or cue helped the scene?
cold_call.higher: Why did you keep that voice and move when the plan changed?

lessons.title: Test a skill for a short performance
lessons.outcome: Develop drama or music skills for performance.
lessons.goal: I can test a drama or sound skill and choose a goal.
success: I can try two versions of one skill.
I can explain a choice for a short piece.
I can set a small practice goal.
words: Something you can improve with practice.
How fast words, moves or beats happen.
A short planned silence or still point.
A sign for a performer to start or stop.

artist_cards.description: The Keeper plans to work at a table. It has moved. The performer says, "The table has moved," pauses for one count, then says, "I can ask for help." One open hand shows the empty space.
artist_cards.prompt: How could the pause help the audience follow the change?
artist_cards.model_answer: The pause comes after the table has moved. It gives the audience time to notice a change before the character chooses a response. Another timing can work if its intention is clear.

artist_cards.description: A sound maker creates four soft steady finger taps, one silent count, two slower taps, then four steady taps. The maker says the break marks a plan changing. This is a new class pattern with no tune or words from another work.
artist_cards.notice: Which part breaks the first pattern?
artist_cards.prompt: How could you change the gap or pace to show your own idea?
artist_cards.model_answer: The silent count and two slower taps break the first four-tap pattern. A longer gap could show waiting; a shorter gap could show a quick choice. Those meanings are the maker's choices, not rules.

ta_focus.Independent: Use the prompt ladder. Record what support was actually used. Return the next choice to the pupil after a first-step model.

lessons.evidence: Keep a dated arts-log entry and a precise observation of a real trial. Record what the pupil performed or directed, the chosen feature, reason, feedback and support actually used. A photograph or recording is optional and follows local consent procedures. No supplied teacher model counts as pupil evidence.
lessons.artist_use_note: The two performance examples are invented classroom demonstrations, not accounts of real artists or an arts encounter. Read or demonstrate them in the room. They can support comparison and skills exploration only.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Choose drama or quiet original sound.
You may perform, direct or work seated.
Our invented story is The changed table.
stages.say: Our half-term theme is Resilience & Change. The Keeper's table has moved. We can show a small change through drama or a new sound pattern. Choose a route and agree the quiet stop signal. We are not sharing real personal changes.
stages.good: Every pupil chooses a route and an access method. Noise and space agreements are explicit.
stages.fallback: Offer a silent hand scene or pupil-directed adult trial. A sound route may be planned and directed without pupil-made sound.
stages.answer: Either art form is valid. A pupil may change route after the first test; record the route actually used.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Watch or hear two versions of a short line or beat.
Which has a pause?
What difference do you notice?
stages.say: I say "The table has moved. I can ask for help" with and without a pause. Or I tap four quiet beats twice, with a gap before the second set. Name what changed, without deciding what it must mean.
stages.good: Pupils notice pace, a gap, stillness or a turn cue and distinguish observation from a possible meaning.
stages.fallback: Use silent finger pulses with a held hand for the gap. Point to gap or no gap.
stages.answer: A pause is an observable feature. "It seems thoughtful to me" is an interpretation. Ask the maker about their intention.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Explore the two original example cards.
Drama uses a line, pause and move.
Sound uses beats, a gap and a pace change.
Choose one skill to test.
stages.say: Read both fictional examples. Demonstrate the drama pause and the sound pattern quietly. My chosen skill is a clear pause. I test one silent count, then two. I choose two so the change is easier to notice. Check after the model: what stayed the same, and what changed?
stages.good: Adult models one variable and a reasoned choice. Pupils identify that the gap length changed while the line or pattern was held stable.
stages.fallback: Demonstrate both gaps with hand pulses. Ask pupil to choose one or two silent counts; adult follows the choice.
stages.answer: The gap changed from one count to two. The other words or beats stayed the same. A longer gap is a choice, not always an improvement.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Pick one shared skill: pause, pace or a turn cue.
Try version A and version B.
Ask: Which fits our idea?
Give a reason based on what changed.
stages.say: In a pair or group of three, agree one choice. For drama, use the Keeper line and test the pause before asking for help. For sound, test the gap between two four-tap groups. Hinge: if we change pace, gap and loudness together, can we tell which helped? Choose one feature to test. If unclear, I hold everything except the gap stable and we compare again.
stages.good: Pupils test one skill at a time and choose with a feature-based reason. Every pupil has a performer, director or listener turn.
stages.fallback: Adult performs the two versions under pupils' direction. Use silent cues and accept pointing for the reason.
stages.answer: Changing one feature makes comparison easier. A useful reason is: the two-count gap made the change easier to hear. Do not require the same interpretation from every pupil.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Choose drama or an original quiet sound pattern.
Pick one skill to practise.
Try two versions. Keep a short trial note.
Choose the version that fits your idea.
Set one small goal for next lesson.
stages.say: Drama: use up to three short original lines about the changed table, with one move or still pause. Sound: create a short pattern of soft taps or silent movements with a planned gap and return. Test one feature twice. A partner describes one feature they noticed. Choose a version, explain why and set a measurable goal such as "hold a two-count pause twice" or "start after the cue twice". Pupils may work in pairs, a three or privately with an adult.
stages.good: Each pupil has two actual trials, one chosen skill and reason, and a small practice goal. Original sound uses no copied tune or lyrics. Directions are retained when an adult performs.
stages.fallback: Choose between one and two silent counts. Adult follows the direction for both trials. Pupil confirms the chosen version and goal; record the evidence as direction.
stages.answer: Example only: I tried one and two silent counts. I chose two to separate the changed plan from the new plan. My goal is to hold that pause in two runs. Do not enter this as a pupil's completed evidence.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Share one short trial with a chosen listener.
Listener: I notice ___.
Maker: I chose ___ because ___.
Store your plan for Wednesday.
stages.say: A whole-class performance is optional. Share a brief section or direct the adult. The listener names a visible or heard feature. The maker can accept, adapt or keep their choice. Use the last two minutes to store dated plans and clear the working area.
stages.good: The pupil's intended effect and practice goal remain their own. The real trial and note are preserved.
stages.fallback: Adult names the observed feature without judgement, then reads the pupil's reason back for confirmation.
stages.answer: Useful feedback identifies a skill: the gap lasted two counts. Avoid diagnosing a character or pupil's feelings.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Log the art form and skill you tried.
Keep your two real versions and reason.
Write, say or show your practice goal.
Record any support you used.
stages.say: Complete the arts log or confirm an adult note. List your two versions, chosen feature and goal. Say if you performed, directed or listened and chose. Keep an honest gap where something was not tried; we can plan a real next step.
stages.good: Dated log includes actual art form, trials, skill choice, reason, measurable next goal and accurate support.
stages.fallback: Adult prompts one item at a time and records exact confirmed words or gesture choices. No recording device is needed.
stages.answer: Example only: I directed a quiet sound pattern with a two-count gap. Next lesson I will cue the return twice. Today's note records direction, not sound performed by the pupil.

Supported: Choose drama or quiet sound with an adult.
Try a one-count and a two-count gap.
Point to the version you want to keep.
Say or show why and pick one practice goal.
Independent: Choose one skill in drama or original sound.
Keep other features the same and test two versions.
Get one notice from a listener and choose a version.
Record a reason and a small goal for lesson two.
Aspire: Set a goal that can be checked in two runs.
Ask for feedback on that skill and explain your choice.
Optional next level: plan who will hear your short piece and what you want to learn from them.

log: I performed / directed / listened and chose ___.
Version A was ___. Version B was ___.
misconceptions: Every test must change the whole piece
Change one feature to compare its effect. Keep a note of the two actual trials.
Music needs a tune or instrument
An original pattern of quiet beats and silence can be explored as sound. Silent movement is an access route.
More sound makes the change clearer
Pace, silence, order and a clear cue can carry the idea without louder sound.
kit: For up to five pupils: one book or arts log and pencil each.
Two invented performance example cards and the short original Keeper lines.
A clear space for pairs or one group of three; seated work is valid.
Hands or fingertips only for optional soft taps; no instrument, playback or device is needed.
Keep the actual trials, chosen feature and practice goal for Wednesday.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Read the Keeper line, using a one-count pause before the help line.
15 to 30 seconds
Repeat with a two-count pause, keeping words and volume the same.
30 to 45 seconds
Show four soft taps, a two-count gap and four soft taps; silent hand pulses can replace taps.
45 to 60 seconds
State a small goal: hold the chosen gap in two runs. Ask a pupil to direct the next version.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Set a specific skill goal for two rehearsal runs. Decide who could listen and what feedback you want on that skill. Explain why that audience can help. You can speak, sketch or write.
stretch.evidence: Keep your own goal, two actual trials and audience plan. Record feedback only when it has really happened; a plan is labelled as a plan.
stretch.why_optional: These additional planning and skills records may support later work at the next level. They are optional for this Explore lesson and do not certify a whole level of the award.
stretch.good: Pupil selects a measurable goal, links it to a real trial and gives a reason for the chosen audience or feedback question.
stretch.fallback: The adult uses the same prompts, performs under the pupil's direction if needed, and records exact confirmed choices and actual support.

models: Teacher model only: I tried one and two silent counts. I kept two because the changed plan was clearer. My goal is to hold two counts in two runs.
Teacher model only: I chose quiet taps and a clear hand cue. I will ask my listener whether the return began together.
lessons.cover: Read and demonstrate the two invented examples, then let pupils choose drama or a quiet original sound pattern. Teach one skill test with two versions and a small goal. Work in pairs or a three with performer, director and listener turns. Keep the genuine trial and goal for Wednesday. Offer silent and private routes throughout.

cold_call.foundation: Where is the pause or gap?
cold_call.middle: What changed between your two trials?
cold_call.higher: How will you know if your skill goal has been met?

lessons.title: Rehearse and refine a short performance
lessons.outcome: Develop drama or music skills for performance.
lessons.goal: I can practise a chosen skill, use feedback and show a refined piece.
success: I can check my skill goal in two runs.
I can test one change after feedback.
I can record my choice and next step.
words: To practise a piece before sharing it.
A useful notice from a listener or viewer.
To make a small change for a clear purpose.
A sign to start, pause or stop.

artist_cards.description: The Keeper plans to work at a table. It has moved. The performer says, "The table has moved," pauses for one count, then says, "I can ask for help." One open hand shows the empty space.
artist_cards.prompt: How could the pause help the audience follow the change?
artist_cards.model_answer: The pause comes after the table has moved. It gives the audience time to notice a change before the character chooses a response. Another timing can work if its intention is clear.

artist_cards.description: A sound maker creates four soft steady finger taps, one silent count, two slower taps, then four steady taps. The maker says the break marks a plan changing. This is a new class pattern with no tune or words from another work.
artist_cards.notice: Which part breaks the first pattern?
artist_cards.prompt: How could you change the gap or pace to show your own idea?
artist_cards.model_answer: The silent count and two slower taps break the first four-tap pattern. A longer gap could show waiting; a shorter gap could show a quick choice. Those meanings are the maker's choices, not rules.

staff_guidance.plain_language: Resilience can mean pausing, asking for help, changing a plan and trying again. It does not mean hiding feelings, tolerating harm or performing through pain.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. The lesson contributes evidence towards the award; it does not confer the award. Optional next level work in GROW adds skills planning, reflection and sharing evidence for later review. It is not a separate requirement for Explore success.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: A clear tiny model is enough. Read the original lines and show a small hand action. Compare two versions. Assess an intentional skill choice and explanation, not acting confidence or a polished performance. Do not use accents, impersonations or a disability to signify a character.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Use the invented changed-table story. No personal story is needed. Offer seated movement, silent direction, a private adult audience and a pass on live peer performance. Voice and taps stay at talking level or below. Agree an open-hand stop signal and quiet return cue. No sudden sounds, contact, running, raised platforms, blindfolds or lifts.
staff_guidance.safety: Clear a small working space. Keep both feet supported if seated. Use hands within each person's own space. No touching another performer or taking a prop from them. Sound is optional; stop on the agreed signal. Pupils can direct the adult to perform their chosen pace and movement. Record that as directed evidence, not a vocal or physical skill the pupil personally demonstrated.
prompt_ladder: Point to the instruction or place.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Pre-teach role, pace, pause and choice with a brief model. Show one instruction at a time. Offer two pace choices, rehearse once, then fade the prompt. Use a tiny plan with beginning, change and response.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Give processing time. Accept pointing to a pace word, signing, a phrase, a sketch or exact words scribed by an adult. Read the record back for confirmation. Do not judge accent, eye contact or facial expression.
adaptations.semh: Keep the story fictional and low stakes. A pause, a change in method or a request for help can be the character's response. Let pupils choose the role, amount of performance and audience. Follow the agreed pause-and-return route.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Offer seated hand movement and no sound. A pupil may direct an adult voice or movement. Keep each person in their own space; use no compulsory facial expression or posture. Ask before handling a pupil's work.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Explain pace as how fast we speak or move. Accept first planning in a familiar language and check the intended meaning before adding English labels. The pupil may use a short English phrase or direct a partner.

misconceptions.claim: A character needs a loud voice or a large action.
misconceptions.correction: A short clear phrase and a small deliberate action can communicate a role. Keep sound at a comfortable level.

misconceptions.claim: Feedback tells a performer what they must feel.
misconceptions.correction: Describe a feature that was seen or heard. Ask the maker about their intention and let them choose a change.

misconceptions.claim: A teacher example can fill a missing arts-log entry.
misconceptions.correction: Record only what the pupil actually chose, tried, directed, made or shared, with the real date and support used.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Performers and sound makers practise a skill, take turns and use feedback to refine a piece.

ta_focus.I do: Make the change in pace or movement easy to notice. Invite a point or sign for the check after the model.
ta_focus.We do: Give each pupil one choice. If the hinge response is uncertain, model one clear contrast before returning to the shared try.
ta_focus.Independent: Use the prompt ladder. Record what support was actually used. Return the next choice to the pupil after a first-step model.

lessons.evidence: Keep a dated arts-log entry and a precise observation of a real trial. Record what the pupil performed or directed, the chosen feature, reason, feedback and support actually used. A photograph or recording is optional and follows local consent procedures. No supplied teacher model counts as pupil evidence.
lessons.artist_use_note: The two performance examples are invented classroom demonstrations, not accounts of real artists or an arts encounter. Read or demonstrate them in the room. They can support comparison and skills exploration only.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your real trial note and goal.
Choose perform, direct or a silent route.
Use the same made-up change story.
stages.say: Use Monday's genuine plan and goal. If you were absent or cannot find it, make a fresh short comparison today and set a goal now. Date that starting point today. We keep the agreed quiet sound level, stop signal and private sharing option.
stages.good: Prior evidence is retrieved accurately or a fresh starting point is recorded. No backfilled claim is made.
stages.fallback: Offer two gap lengths or turn cues; adult demonstrates and pupil confirms a goal.
stages.answer: A new starting point is valid. Do not claim a previous trial or meeting of a goal without evidence.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: State or point to your skill goal.
Show the chosen cue or pause once.
Ask a partner to watch that feature.
stages.say: Rehearse only the feature first. A two-count gap can be shown silently; a turn cue can be a small hand lift. Ask the listener to notice the selected skill rather than rate the whole performance.
stages.good: Pupils recall or confirm one observable goal and ask for focused feedback.
stages.fallback: Adult performs under the pupil's direction and the pupil selects the feature for the listener to notice.
stages.answer: A focused goal can be checked: start after the cue in two runs. "Be better" needs a more precise skill to notice.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch a short first run.
Hear one useful notice.
See one change and a second run.
How can we check the skill?
stages.say: I perform the original Keeper scene or sound pattern. The listener says, "The return began before your cue." I test a clearer hand cue, then repeat. I count one successful start, not two. Check: is my goal met if it asked for two runs? What real evidence do I still need?
stages.good: Adult models honest checking, one refinement and a real second attempt. Pupils distinguish partial progress from a fully checked goal.
stages.fallback: Show two silent hand starts and ask pupils to point to together or early. Keep a visible count of actual runs.
stages.answer: One successful start is progress but does not meet a goal of two successful starts. Complete a second real run or record the goal as still in progress.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Try the shared piece once.
Listener names the chosen skill.
Choose one change and repeat.
Check what really happened.
stages.say: Use the same short changed-table story. Let one person cue, one perform and one observe; in a pair, the adult can observe. Hinge: if a listener says "The gap was one count," but our plan says two, should we write two because it was planned? If anyone is unsure, model and count the real gap together before another try.
stages.good: Pupils use feedback about an actual feature and record the trial honestly. They understand that a plan is different from observed evidence.
stages.fallback: Adult follows a pupil cue; another pupil points to one or two counts. Share privately if preferred.
stages.answer: Record one count for that run. Try again if wanted. Never replace observed evidence with the intended plan. The maker decides what to change.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Rehearse your drama or original sound piece.
Check the skill in two real runs.
Get one useful notice.
Test one change, or explain why you keep it.
Share a short final version with a chosen listener.
stages.say: Use up to three short lines or a brief original beat-and-gap pattern. Keep the focus on your selected skill. Do a first run, hear one feature notice, then choose one adjustment in pace, pause, movement or cue. Try the adjusted version and check your goal. If the new choice is less useful, return to the first and explain why. Swap performer, director and listener roles so each pupil makes a real choice. Whole-class performance is optional.
stages.good: A genuine rehearsal, feature-based feedback and tested refinement or justified kept choice are recorded. Each pupil contributes an intentional skill choice and checks the goal honestly. A directed piece is labelled as directed.
stages.fallback: Pupil directs the adult's two runs by selecting a gap or cue. Adult records the direction, observed result and exact confirmed reason. Silent hand movement can carry all cues.
stages.answer: Example only: The first start was early. I made the cue clearer and we began together in the next run. My goal is partly met; I need one more successful run. Alternatively record two successes only if both occurred.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Share your final short version or direct it.
Listener: I notice ___.
Maker: I changed or kept ___ because ___.
Put plans and real notes in order.
stages.say: Invite a chosen listener to name one feature they saw or heard. The maker links a kept or changed choice to the intended effect. If time permits one final check, do it; otherwise record the next step honestly. Use the last two minutes to clear the space and store logs.
stages.good: Pupils communicate a reasoned choice and retain feedback that actually happened. Goal status is clear.
stages.fallback: Adult acts as private listener and reads the confirmed choice note back. No public performance or recording is required.
stages.answer: Useful reflection links a change to its purpose: the longer pause gave the new plan a clear start. A goal still in progress is a valid honest outcome.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Log your two real runs and feedback.
Say what you changed or kept, and why.
Mark goal met, partly met or next time.
Choose one next step for next week's story.
stages.say: Keep the actual plan, trial notes and confirmed reflection together. Include your art form, what you performed or directed, listener notice, choice, goal status and support. Next week we will use a short sequence about overcoming a change; a clear cue or pause can carry forward.
stages.good: Dated record shows real evidence of practice and reflection, an accurate goal judgement and a concrete next step.
stages.fallback: Prompt one item at a time. Record a short witnessed note and let the pupil correct it. Leave an honest gap rather than filling it with the teacher model.
stages.answer: Example only: I directed the pause. One run had two counts and one had one count. I will practise holding two counts before the final line.

Supported: Find or make one small skill goal.
Direct or try two short runs with an adult.
Hear one notice and choose a change.
Confirm a real note of what happened.
Independent: Use your chosen drama or sound route.
Check your goal in two actual runs.
Test one change after focused feedback.
Log the result, reason and next step.
Aspire: Complete the same core rehearsal and log.
Compare the first and refined version in detail.
Explain how your skill choice helps the intended audience.
Optional next level: lead a short feedback turn and record what you learned from the actual exchange.

log: My art form and skill were ___.
Run one showed ___. Run two showed ___.
My goal is met / partly met / still to try because ___.
misconceptions: A planned skill is evidence that it happened
Keep the plan and the observation distinct. Record what really happened in each run.
Every suggestion must be used
Test one useful suggestion, then keep or change it for a reason.
A goal in progress means the piece failed
Progress and a clear next step are useful evidence of practice. Do not invent a completed goal.
kit: For up to five pupils: books or arts logs, pencils, Monday's actual trial notes and goals if available.
Original changed-table scene lines or pupil-made quiet beat-and-gap plans.
Clear space for pairs or a group of three; no contact, costumes, devices or instruments required.
A listener may be the adult; a private or silent directed route remains available.
Store the initial plan, trial results and confirmed reflection together for the ongoing arts log.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show a brief first run, starting the return before the agreed cue.
15 to 30 seconds
Listener says: I notice the return began before the cue. Show a clearer hand cue.
30 to 45 seconds
Repeat and check what happened. Count the real successful run only.
45 to 60 seconds
Say: That is one success. My goal asks for two; I need one more real run or an honest next step.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Compare two runs of your scene or beat. What got clearer? Which change helped? Say what you kept and why. Set one small skill goal and a way to check it.
stretch.evidence: Keep a note of both runs and your own part. Add the real feedback, your choice and reason. Add your next skill goal.
stretch.why_optional: These extra skills, sharing and reflection records may support later work at the next level. They are optional for Explore and do not certify all requirements of the award.
stretch.good: Pupil leads an accessible exchange, selects evidence from actual runs and explains how the feedback informed a choice or next step.
stretch.fallback: Use a private adult listener. Pupil points or speaks while adult scribes and reads the record back. Record directing separately from performing.

models: Teacher model only: Our first return was early. We made the hand cue clearer and began together. I need one more real run to check my two-run goal.
Teacher model only: I kept the quiet pace after testing a faster version. My listener could follow the change more easily. I will use that pause in our next story.
lessons.cover: Retrieve genuine plans and goals or make a fresh dated test. Model focused feedback, one tested change and honest checking over two real runs. Let pupils choose drama or quiet original sound with the same change story. Rotate performer, director and listener turns, keep silent/private routes available, then record the actual goal status and next step.

cold_call.middle: What did your listener actually notice?
cold_call.higher: Which evidence shows your goal is met or still in progress?

scope: Explore for both pathways. Optional GROW next level stretch retains additional evidence without changing core success criteria.
timing: Arrival 0-3; Starter 3-6; I do 6-12; We do 12-18; Create 18-32; Review 32-37; Exit 37-40 minutes.
